newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan shilling weakens against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan shilling weakens against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened slightly against the dollar on Monday as speculators bought dollars, dealers said.
Commercial bank dealers said the shilling eased to a mean commercial rate of 69 compared to Monday's opening of 68.87 and Friday's close of 69.02.
The shilling sunk to an official record low against the dollar at 70.26 on Thursday, extending losses begun after the International Monetary Fund halted a key aid package on July 31.

"The shilling is beginning to display further signs of weakening after opening strong relative to last week's closing," said a dealer. "A few people rushed in to buy after they saw the shilling was at 69 levels."
Investors were buying at between 69.50 and 70.50, dealers said. The shilling edged up against the dollar on Friday as exporters sold dollars following the shilling's record fall.
Market analysts expected the shilling to consolidate this week as investors assessed the market. "What we have is a breathing space, not a reprieve," said an analyst from Loita Asset Management.
"Today (Monday) is a traditionally thin day for exporters so any dollar demand will be exaggerated," one dealer said.
